Use the metric description of the uniformity for the first conjunct: entourages are generated by sets of pairs at distance \(<\varepsilon\). Unfolding `TendstoUniformlyOnFilter` then turns the nested eventuality over \(p\) and \(p'\) into one eventuality over the product filter \(p \timesˢ p'\), giving exactly the stated \(\varepsilon\)-criterion.

For the second conjunct, name its two sides \(A\) and \(B\) and prove both independently; they are unrelated universal facts, so the final equivalence follows because both are true.

- For \(A\), work locally at each \(x\in s\). Use `hf` and `hg` to choose a common neighborhood on which \(f\) and \(g\) are bounded. Local uniform convergence makes \(F_i-f\) and \(G_i-g\) uniformly small there and consequently bounds the approximants as well. Apply the quantitative estimate supplied by `IsBoundedSMul` to
  \[
  d(F_i(y)\smul G_i(y),\,f(y)\smul g(y)),
  \]
  splitting the error into a small difference multiplied by a bounded factor. This proves locally uniform convergence of the pointwise smuls.

- For \(B\), use that unconditional summability of a real family implies summability of its absolute values. Since
  \[
  \operatorname{toNNReal}(f(n))=\max(f(n),0)\le |f(n)|,
  \]
  comparison yields summability of the resulting `NNReal` family.

The essential hypotheses are precisely local boundedness for the smul estimate and unconditional summation for the passage from \(f\) to its positive part.
